newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan stock futures to help Taiwan markets.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan stock futures to help Taiwan markets.

text.p: The launch of Taiwan stock index futures and options on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) on Thursday will benefit Taiwan's domestic stock market, a SIMEX official said.
SIMEX president Ang Swee Tian said the contract would "help accelerate the internationalisation" of the Taiwan stock market.
Ang told reporters he did not expect Taiwanese regulators to block access to price data after reviewing trading on the contracts in Singapore and Chicago.

"I personally really doubt that that would be a move they would really make," he said, noting that SIMEX was still holding talks with Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission to show it was open to cooperation between the two countries.
The Taiwan stock index futures contract got off to a slow and cautious start on SIMEX on Thursday, hamstrung by Taiwan regulators warning its investors not to trade, dealers said.
A mere 370 contracts changed hands in the first hour.

The SIMEX futures and options contracts are based on the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) Taiwan index, which is a market capitalisation-weighted index of 77 component stocks covering 67 percent of Taiwan's stock market.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) launched futures and options contracts based on the Dow Jones Taiwan stock index five minutes after SIMEX MSCI Taiwan index futures began trading at 0055 GMT.
Taiwanese regulators said on Saturday they did not rule out the possibility of cutting the supply of data to SIMEX or the CME after a six-month review.
Ang said SIMEX had been holding talks with Taiwanese authorities over the last six years about its desire to establish a futures contract based on the Taiwan stock index.

SIMEX decided to go ahead with the contract, despite Taiwan's pleas for a delay until Taipei had built its own futures infrastructure, after Chicago announced plans to launch a Taiwan stock index futures contract, Ang said.
"I was in Taiwan to explain that we cannot hold on due to the U.S. markets launching the contract. We had to take on the challenge and meet the demands of our international members," Ang said.
He said SIMEX welcomed the establishment of a futures exchange in Taiwan as this would benefit the international market.
SIMEX chairman Victor Liew said the SIMEX contract was likely to do well as it would trade during Asian time on an open outcry system, as opposed to electronic trading on GLOBEX in Chicago.
He said SIMEX and CME had decided to launch separate contracts despite their long-standing tradition of cooperation as they had not been able to agree on several issues.
